result.title: Data-Driven Glyph Positioning for Handwritten Music Synthesis
result.comment: 10 pages, 1 biblio page, presented at The 20th International Conference on Document Analysis and Recognition
result.summary: Synthesised data is a common strategy to address the lack of annotated handwritten music scores in Optical Music Recognition (OMR). Smashcima is a recent synthesis framework that assembles pages of handwritten scores by sampling glyph images from MUSCIMA++ and positioning them with hard-coded rules. In this work we ask whether these rules are grounded empirically and whether a learned model for context-dependent positioning can further improve synthesis quality. We extract inter-glyph distributions from around 285 thousand annotated relationships across MUSCIMA++ and OmniOMR, finding that several key parameters deviate systematically from real handwriting. Replacing these constants with empirical means reduces positioning RMSE by up to 60%. We then train a Graph Neural Network (GNN) on the Music Notation Graph structure to predict context-dependent offsets, achieving an additional 50 to 85% RMSE reduction on stems and beams by modelling how neighbouring glyphs constrain placement. Cross-dataset analysis shows that spacing differences between the two corpora are explained by note density (3.3), not style, and that duration-proportional spacing does not hold in handwriting (R2 = 0.001). In downstream evaluation, a YOLOv8 detector pretrained on GNN-positioned synthetic data achieves +30% mAP50 over the baseline and +11% over empirical means when fine-tuned on 200 real handwritten staves, showing that positioning accuracy matters for downstream OMR.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文针对手写乐谱合成，从 MUSCIMA++ 与 OmniOMR 中统计字形间距分布，指出 Smashcima 的硬编码定位规则偏离真实手写，再用 GNN 依据 Music Notation Graph 预测上下文相关偏移，并以下游 OMR 检测器性能验证合成质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作属于文档图像合成与合成数据质量改进，不涉及 latent 推理状态、视觉证据筛选或停止决策；其 GNN 建模的是页面内字形摆放约束而非模型内部表示，与 LVR 主线缺少可核查的实质联系。
